prompt: In which sentence does "sanction" mean "officially approve"?

options.text: The board sanctioned the new pay scale after a long debate.
The alliance sanctioned the country for breaching the treaty.
Several trading partners imposed sanctions on the exporter.
The sanctions were lifted once the inspectors were admitted.

explanation: sanction 是少見的「反義同形字」：當及物動詞用於規則、決策時是「批准」，用於國家或個人時是「制裁」，名詞複數 sanctions 幾乎一律是「制裁」。這裡董事會核准薪資級距，屬於「批准」。

distractorExplanations.b: 這裡的 sanction 是「制裁、處罰」，因為對象是違約的國家。
distractorExplanations.c: 名詞複數 sanctions 指「制裁措施」，不是批准。
distractorExplanations.d: lift sanctions 是「解除制裁」，同樣是處罰的意思。

options.text: Heavy rain impeded the rescue effort for two days.
The manager impeded the report to the board on Friday.
She impeded from the meeting before it ended.
They impeded the contract for another twelve months.

explanation: impede 是及物動詞「妨礙、拖慢（進行中的事）」，主詞常是造成阻礙的因素。

distractorExplanations.b: 把報告送交董事會要用 submit 或 present。
distractorExplanations.c: 提早離開會議要用 withdraw from 或 leave；impede 不接 from。
distractorExplanations.d: 延長合約要用 extend 或 renew。

options.text: The airline curtailed its overseas routes to cut costs.
He curtailed the door quietly behind him as he left.
We curtailed the old files into a single archive.
The train curtailed at every small station on the line.

explanation: curtail 是「縮減（規模、範圍、權利、支出）」，受詞是抽象的量或活動。

distractorExplanations.b: 關門要用 closed 或 pulled shut。
distractorExplanations.c: 把檔案合併要用 consolidated 或 merged。
distractorExplanations.d: 列車停靠要用 stopped；curtail 也不能當不及物動詞。

options.text: She augmented her income with freelance editing.
He augmented the meeting until Thursday afternoon.
The nurse augmented him a painkiller before the scan.
They augmented from the agreement without warning.

explanation: augment 是正式用語「增添、補強（既有的量）」，常見於 augment income／staff／data。

distractorExplanations.b: 延後會議要用 postpone 或 push back。
distractorExplanations.c: 給藥要用 gave 或 administered；augment 不接雙受詞。
distractorExplanations.d: 退出協議要用 withdrew from；augment 是及物動詞。

options.text: The new evidence bolstered their case considerably.
The runner bolstered past the finish line in first place.
She bolstered the letter into the envelope and sealed it.
The committee bolstered him of any responsibility.

explanation: bolster 是「支撐、強化（論點、信心、需求）」，受詞多半是抽象事物。

distractorExplanations.b: bolster 不是移動動詞；衝過終點線要用 surged 或 raced。
distractorExplanations.c: 把信放進信封要用 slipped 或 put。
distractorExplanations.d: 免除責任要用 cleared him of 或 absolved him of。

options.text: He kept meticulous records of every transaction.
The weather stayed meticulous for the whole trip.
She was meticulous to catch the early train.
They arrived meticulous at the airport with time to spare.

explanation: meticulous 形容「極度仔細、一絲不苟的（人或其成果）」，常搭配 records、planning、attention to detail。

distractorExplanations.b: 天氣要用 fine 或 glorious；meticulous 不形容天氣。
distractorExplanations.c: 「很想趕上早班車」要用 eager 或 anxious。
distractorExplanations.d: meticulous 不能當副詞修飾 arrived。

options.text: Further negotiation proved futile, so the talks were called off.
The soup tasted futile without any salt in it.
He felt futile about his colleague's promotion.
The motorway was futile with holiday traffic.

explanation: futile 形容「注定沒有結果的（努力、嘗試）」，常見搭配是 futile attempt／effort／gesture。

distractorExplanations.b: 湯沒味道要用 bland 或 tasteless。
distractorExplanations.c: 對同事升遷的心情要用 resentful 或 envious。
distractorExplanations.d: 路上塞車要用 clogged 或 congested。

options.text: Most of the job involves mundane administrative tasks.
The mundane storm tore the roof off the barn.
He was mundane with anger after reading the email.
They mundane the same report every quarter.

explanation: mundane 是「平淡無奇、例行的」，用來形容日常瑣事。

distractorExplanations.b: 猛烈的暴風雨要用 violent 或 severe。
distractorExplanations.c: 氣得發抖要用 shaking with anger；mundane 不表示情緒。
distractorExplanations.d: mundane 是形容詞，不能當動詞用。

options.text: The sensor gave erratic readings all morning.
She was erratic to help us with the move.
The book was erratic of useful examples.
He erratic the schedule twice a week.

explanation: erratic 形容「時好時壞、毫無規律的」，常搭配 readings、behaviour、performance。

distractorExplanations.b: 樂意幫忙要用 willing 或 happy to help。
distractorExplanations.c: 「充滿實用範例」要用 full of；erratic 不接 of。
distractorExplanations.d: erratic 是形容詞，不能當動詞；改變時程要用 changed。

options.text: The sudden silence in the control room felt ominous.
The cake was ominous and everyone asked for more.
She was ominous with the good news all afternoon.
They ominous the storm warning the day before.

explanation: ominous 是「不祥的、預示壞事的」，形容氣氛、跡象、雲層等。

distractorExplanations.c: 帶著好消息很開心要用 delighted 或 thrilled。
distractorExplanations.d: ominous 是形容詞，不能當動詞；發布警報要用 issued。

options.text: In a candid interview, she admitted the project had failed.
The candid weather made the outdoor concert a success.
He was candid of the train times before we set off.
They candid their opinion at the end of the meeting.

explanation: candid 是「坦率、不避諱地說出實情的」，常搭配 candid interview／assessment／conversation。

distractorExplanations.b: 天氣晴朗要用 fine 或 clear。
distractorExplanations.c: 「清楚知道班車時刻」要用 aware of 或 sure of。
distractorExplanations.d: candid 是形容詞；表達意見要用 voiced 或 gave。

options.text: A long argument ensued, and the meeting overran by an hour.
They ensued a long argument for almost an hour.
The committee was ensued by a long argument.
She ensued to the argument as politely as she could.

explanation: ensue 是不及物動詞「（隨後）發生」，主詞就是後來發生的那件事，不接受詞，也沒有被動式。

distractorExplanations.b: ensue 不能接受詞；要說 An argument ensued。
distractorExplanations.d: ensue 不接 to；禮貌回應要用 responded to。

options.text: Younger designers try to emulate her use of colour.
The printer emulated to work again after a restart.
He emulated with his brother over the prize.
She emulated from the competition after one round.

explanation: emulate 是及物動詞「效法、以……為榜樣（並設法達到同樣水準）」。

distractorExplanations.b: 機器恢復運作要用 started working；emulate 不接不定詞。
distractorExplanations.c: 與人競爭要用 competed with；emulate 不接 with。
distractorExplanations.d: 退出比賽要用 withdrew from。

options.text: The injury rendered him unable to play for a whole season.
The injury rendered to him unable to play for a season.
The injury rendered that he was unable to play for a season.
The injury rendered him for unable to play for a season.

explanation: render somebody/something + 形容詞 表示「使……變成某狀態」，受詞後面直接接形容詞，中間不加介系詞或連接詞。

distractorExplanations.b: render 不接 to；受詞直接跟在動詞後面。
distractorExplanations.c: render 不接 that 子句。
